text: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation throughout his whole kingdom, and also put it in writing:
"This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
Whoever among you belongs to his people—may his God be with him—let him go up to Jerusalem in Judah and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel, the God who is in Jerusalem.

And everyone who remains, wherever he lives, let the people of that place support him with silver and gold, with goods and livestock, along with a freewill offering for the house of God in Jerusalem."
Then the heads of the families of Judah and Benjamin, along with the priests and the Levites—everyone whose spirit God had stirred—set out to go up and build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.
And all their neighbors strengthened their hands with articles of silver and gold, with goods and livestock and valuable gifts, besides all the freewill offerings.

versions.text: And all their neighbors supported them with articles of silver and gold, with goods and livestock and valuable gifts, besides all the freewill offerings.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew idiom 'strengthened their hands' is vivid and distinct from the verb used in v.4 (יְנַשְּׂאוּהוּ, 'support'); using 'supported' in both verses flattens the difference. Either rendering works, but retaining the idiom (or 'assisted') avoids the repetition.

text: King Cyrus also brought out the articles of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had carried off from Jerusalem and placed in the temple of his own god.
Cyrus king of Persia had them brought out by Mithredath the treasurer, who counted them out to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.
This was the inventory: thirty gold basins, a thousand silver basins, twenty-nine knives,*

versions.text: This was the inventory: thirty gold basins, a thousand silver basins, twenty-nine knives,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew word מַחֲלָפִים occurs only here and its meaning is uncertain (often rendered 'knives' or 'censers'/'duplicates'). A brief footnote noting the uncertainty would help the reader.

text: thirty gold bowls, four hundred and ten silver bowls of a second kind, and a thousand other articles.

versions.text: thirty gold bowls, four hundred and ten matching silver bowls, and a thousand other articles.
versions.explanation: מִשְׁנִים most likely designates a second/lesser grade or class of bowl rather than bowls 'matching' one another; 'matching' could mislead the hearer into thinking they matched the gold bowls.

text: In all there were five thousand four hundred articles of gold and silver. Sheshbazzar brought all of these up with the exiles when they came from Babylon to Jerusalem.
